headline: Profit surges on tax gain as core earnings hold flat
summary_short: Net income of $1,298 million (+30.5% y/y, +51.6% q/q) reflects a $251 million tax benefit tied to the pending sale of Hartford Funds; core earnings, which exclude that gain, rose a more modest 1% to $945 million ($3.42 core EPS) as diluted EPS reached $4.68.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $7,263 million (+8.3% y/y) on 5% premium growth in both Business Insurance and Employee Benefits. Net income jumped 30.5% y/y to $1,298 million, lifted by a $251 million tax benefit tied to the pending Hartford Funds sale and $64 million of realized gains; core earnings, which exclude those items, rose just 1% to $945 million. Business Insurance's combined ratio widened to 91.4 from 87.0 on less-favorable reserve development and higher catastrophe losses, while Personal Insurance's improved to 90.1. Employee Benefits' core margin compressed to 7.4% on a higher disability loss ratio. Cash fell to $203 million q/q after $450 million of buybacks; book value per diluted share rose 6.0% since year-end to $70.28.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed drivers: 5% premium growth in Business Insurance and Employee Benefits; net income lifted by a tax benefit and realized gains tied to the pending Hartford Funds sale; Business Insurance's combined ratio widened on less-favorable reserve development while Personal Insurance's improved.

Continuing-operations pretax income rose only 4.9% y/y ($1,231M vs $1,174M); nearly all of net income's 30.5% y/y jump is explained by discontinued operations (Hartford Funds sale), which contributed $318M after tax vs $57M a year earlier, including a $251M tax benefit.
EPS growth (+36.0%) outpaces net income growth (+30.5%) because weighted diluted shares fell 4.0% y/y on ongoing share buybacks.
Company attributes growth to 5% written-premium growth in Business Insurance (led by Small Business) and 5% fully insured ongoing premium growth in Employee Benefits.
Company attributes book value growth mainly to net income in excess of stockholder dividends, partly offset by the dilutive effect of share repurchases and a decrease in AOCI from higher rates.
Company disclosed $450 million of shares repurchased in the quarter as part of returning $615 million to stockholders, reducing share count.
